From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). ## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer playbook. The most serious points are:

1. materially weaker warranty cap, thresholds and claims period without required Buyer approval;
2. improper application of the general limitations regime to title, fundamental warranties, indemnities, covenants and payment obligations;
3. no fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out;
4. ineffective Bluefen consent mechanics;
5. post-Completion Riverlark repayment/release risk;
6. broad deemed disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions;
7. unallocated employee bonus and on-cost exposure;
8. an unduly narrow Ironquay indemnity; and
9. unsupported assertions that tax, IP and certain diligence matters are resolved or immaterial.

The Disclosure Letter is more cautious than the Seller Update and confirms several unresolved matters. Its factual statements are not evidence that the associated risks have been cured or accepted.

## Detailed review

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** Our starting position is 25%, or AUD 6 million. The 20% cap is only a conditional fallback requiring prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the relevant draft. No such approval has been given.

**Pushback:**

- Restore the AUD 6 million cap.
- Do not describe 20% as agreed or cleared merely because it matches an internal fallback.
- Limit this cap to properly defined general warranty claims only.
- Expressly exclude title/fundamental claims, fraud-related matters, specific indemnities, tax claims, price/payment obligations and covenant claims from this general cap, subject to their separately negotiated regimes.

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only excess over the basket recoverable.

**Departure:** Our position is:

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- a tipping basket, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller’s proposal is five times each agreed threshold and converts the basket into a deductible. It could eliminate recovery for a substantial collection of genuine claims.

**Pushback:** Reinstate the Buyer thresholds and first-dollar recovery. Ensure excluded categories, including title/fundamental claims and specific indemnities, are not subjected to either threshold.

### 3. General claims period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Departure:** Our position is 24 months. Eighteen months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate 24 months. Also ensure timely notification preserves the claim until finally resolved and that technical defects in a notice do not invalidate it unless the Seller is materially prejudiced.

### 4. Fundamental, title and capacity claims

**Seller position:** Same cap and time limits as general warranties “for administrative simplicity.”

**Departure:** This directly conflicts with the required separate regime:

- 100% of the purchase price cap;
- at least six years after Completion; and
- no general de minimis, basket or Buyer-knowledge exclusion.

Administrative convenience is not a basis for transferring ownership risk to the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Create an express separate category covering title, ownership, capacity, authority and valid issuance of shares. It should have a 100% cap and at least a six-year claims period and sit outside the general thresholds and knowledge limitations.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance

**Seller position:** These provisions apply to all claims of any nature.

**Departure:** This is an unacceptable hidden override of separately negotiated protections. It could limit:

- title and capacity claims;
- tax claims;
- IP claims and specific indemnities;
- payment and purchase price obligations;
- pre- and post-Completion covenants; and
- claims involving fraud or intentional wrongdoing.

**Pushback:**

- Confine the general limitations to general warranty claims.
- Create clear, separate regimes for title/fundamental, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant breaches.
- Do not permit a broad definition of “Claim” or a general “notwithstanding” clause to pull those categories back under the general regime.
- Preserve all non-excludable statutory rights and remedies.

### 6. Mandatory misconduct carve-outs

The Seller package does not provide the required protection.

**Pushback:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of:

- all caps;
- de minimis and baskets;
- time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions;
- non-reliance provisions; and
- knowledge and disclosure limitations,

in each case to the maximum extent enforceable. This point is not waivable under the Buyer playbook.

### 7. General disclosure and deemed disclosure

**Seller position:** The entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records are generally disclosed.

**Departure:** We require specific fair disclosure. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure is unacceptable because it transfers to the Buyer the burden of identifying the relevance and consequences of documents.

The specific disclosures in paragraphs 2–10 may be considered individually, but only against the precise warranty they are said to qualify and only if they fairly disclose the nature and reasonably apparent scope of the matter. Merely citing a document number is not necessarily enough.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosure.
- Require each disclosure to identify the relevant warranty, facts, scope, amount where known, and operative document provisions.
- State that disclosure is effective only where specifically and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception.
- Require a refreshed disclosure package and data-room index. The stated cut-off is 22 September 2026 and is now stale.
- Require a Completion bring-down and disclosure of material developments since the cut-off.

Paragraph 1.4’s non-admission wording can remain only if it does not dilute the fair-disclosure standard or convert uncertainty into an effective blanket disclosure.

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is both an actual and constructive knowledge bar and would undermine the warranties and the required disclosure process.

**Pushback:**

- Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
- Reject deemed knowledge from advisers, the data room, public records or matters that a “prudent” Buyer might have discovered.
- Any knowledge-qualified Seller warranty should instead refer to specifically named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
- No knowledge limitation may excuse title, capacity, fraud-related matters or a specific indemnity.

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue, around 30%. There is no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** Reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer consent. Delivery of a document is not enough if the consent is conditional, ineffective or its conditions remain unsatisfied.

**Pushback:**

- Make Completion conditional on receipt of an effective written consent in an agreed form.
- Require evidence before Completion that all conditions to that consent have been satisfied or validly waived.
- Ensure the consent is not revocable and does not impose unacceptable amendments, payments, concessions or termination rights.
- Buyer alone should determine whether the condition has been satisfied or waived.

This is a likely Completion blocker unless properly cured.

### 10. Riverlark facility and security

**Facts:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding. There is no final security discharge.

**Seller position:** Release following Completion.

**Departure:** The acquisition is debt-free/cash-free. The Buyer should not acquire the company while Riverlark debt and security remain outstanding.

**Pushback:**

- Obtain a current payout letter, not an approximate historical balance.
- Repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds.
- Require effective releases and discharges of all guarantees, security interests and related claims at Completion.
- Confirm required change-of-control treatment.
- Include clear funds-flow directions and evidence of lodgement or control of necessary discharge documentation.

A post-Completion release is unacceptable unless supported by an irrevocable undertaking and specifically approved by Amelia Frost. No such approval currently exists.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts:** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. They are absent from the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** They are a matter for the Seller but need not be itemised.

**Departure:** Silence in the funds flow creates a risk that the target or Buyer funds a Seller transaction cost after Completion.

**Pushback:**

- Quantify all bonuses and triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- Include them as a specific line item in the funds flow or require separate Seller funding.
- Specify who pays, when payment occurs, and the treatment of employees who cease to satisfy a condition.
- Obtain evidence of payment and satisfaction of associated withholding and contribution obligations.
- Prevent double counting through another debt or working-capital adjustment.

The Seller’s statement that the amounts are “a matter for the Seller” is not adequate without operative SPA and funds-flow mechanics.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this has not been independently verified. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** A payment-only indemnity may not protect against failure of title, non-vesting of rights, infringement allegations, enforcement costs, business disruption or consequential remediation.

**Pushback:**

- Verify the amount directly and obtain an up-to-date statement or confirmation from Ironquay.
- Require payment and documentary confirmation that all relevant IP has vested or been assigned.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from non-payment, failure of assignment or vesting, third-party ownership or infringement claims, and reasonable cure and enforcement costs.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism so the Seller can cure through cleared payment and effective transfer.
- Keep the Ironquay indemnity outside the general warranty basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Negotiate its cap and duration as a distinct IP matter; do not assume either unlimited liability or that it is resolved under the general regime.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts:** An export link was sent to an unintended external email address and may cover approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and notification obligations remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The Disclosure Letter correctly stops short of establishing access, a confirmed breach, notification duty or loss. We should not assert any of those matters without evidence. Equally, the Seller’s expectation of immateriality is unsupported and should not close the issue.

**Pushback:**

- Require immediate preservation of logs, emails, access records, exported files and investigation materials.
- Require a properly scoped investigation and regular written updates.
- Require prompt notice of access evidence, affected data, regulator or individual communications, containment steps and any legal assessment of notification duties.
- Prohibit deletion or alteration of relevant evidence.
- Allocate responsibility for pre-Completion investigation and remediation without assuming a numeric claim or price deduction at this stage.
- Preserve relevant warranties and remedies; do not allow the general disclosure to neutralise them before the facts are known.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts:** Three renewals total AUD 330,000. The current record does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That characterisation is not established by the disclosed facts. Conversely, the amount should not automatically be treated as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Review the renewal terms, service periods, invoices, cancellation rights, accounting treatment, timing and consistency with historical practice. Then determine whether the amounts belong in normal working capital, are Seller obligations, or require another specific adjustment. Avoid both automatic Debt classification and untested acceptance as ordinary course.

### 15. Tax and general IP positions

**Seller position:** Settled under the general regime.

**Departure:** Tax and IP remain open. A counterparty assertion does not settle them, and the general regime must not silently govern them.

**Pushback:**

- Continue separate negotiation of the tax covenant, tax warranties, IP warranties and relevant indemnities.
- Ensure no general clause overrides their separately agreed caps, periods, thresholds or procedures.
- Do not assume unlimited liability, but equally do not accept the proposed general cap and 18-month period by default.

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves ownership of 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof of title, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:** Require a complete title package, including, as applicable:

- share certificates and issuance/transfer history;
- consistency checks against corporate filings and constitution;
- Seller corporate approvals and execution authority;
- searches and releases concerning security interests or other encumbrances;
- confirmation of no options, convertibles, trusts, beneficial interests or third-party rights; and
- Completion transfers and updated registers.

This evidence supplements rather than replaces the title warranties and 100% fundamental liability regime.

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale

The current disclosures indicate only:

- an office lease notification obligation, not necessarily landlord consent; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction that may not be engaged by a share sale.

We should verify the operative language and comply with any notice requirements, but should not assume consents or price adjustments are required merely from the Seller’s document descriptions. Appropriate no-breach and contracts warranties should remain.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Completion-critical items

1. Effective Bluefen consent, with all conditions satisfied and evidenced.
2. Current Riverlark payout, direct repayment and effective releases at Completion.
3. Clear Seller-funded treatment of the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all triggered on-costs.
4. Ironquay payment/title cure and a broadened specific indemnity.
5. Updated investigation, evidence preservation and reporting for the export/privacy incident.
6. Independent title and encumbrance evidence.

### SPA liability package

1. AUD 6 million general warranty cap.
2. AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
3. Twenty-four-month general claims period.
4. Separate 100%/six-year minimum title and fundamental regime.
5. Mandatory fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs.
6. General limitations confined to general warranties.
7. Separate treatment for tax, IP, specific indemnities, payments and covenants.

### Disclosure and diligence

1. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and constructive disclosure.
2. Delete the broad Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
3. Assess each specific disclosure against the relevant warranty and fair-disclosure standard.
4. Refresh the data room and disclosures through Completion.
5. Investigate Sandbar without automatically treating it as either Debt or ordinary-course cost.

None of the Seller’s descriptions—“agreed,” “adequate,” “settled,” “ordinary course” or “not expected to be material”—should be treated as an agreed Buyer position or verified factual conclusion.

- Include clear funds-flow directions and evidence of lodgement or control of necessary discharge documentation.

A post-Completion release is unacceptable unless supported by an irrevocable undertaking and specifically approved by Amelia Frost. No such approval currently exists.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts:** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. They are absent from the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** They are a matter for the Seller but need not be itemised.

**Departure:** Silence in the funds flow creates a risk that the target or Buyer funds a Seller transaction cost after Completion.

**Pushback:**

- Quantify all bonuses and triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- Include them as a specific line item in the funds flow or require separate Seller funding.
- Specify who pays, when payment occurs, and the treatment of employees who cease to satisfy a condition.
- Obtain evidence of payment and satisfaction of associated withholding and contribution obligations.
- Prevent double counting through another debt or working-capital adjustment.

The Seller’s statement that the amounts are “a matter for the Seller” is not adequate without operative SPA and funds-flow mechanics.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this has not been independently verified. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** A payment-only indemnity may not protect against failure of title, non-vesting of rights, infringement allegations, enforcement costs, business disruption or consequential remediation.

**Pushback:**

- Verify the amount directly and obtain an up-to-date statement or confirmation from Ironquay.
- Require payment and documentary confirmation that all relevant IP has vested or been assigned.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from non-payment, failure of assignment or vesting, third-party ownership or infringement claims, and reasonable cure and enforcement costs.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism so the Seller can cure through cleared payment and effective transfer.
- Keep the Ironquay indemnity outside the general warranty basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Negotiate its cap and duration as a distinct IP matter; do not assume either unlimited liability or that it is resolved under the general regime.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts:** An export link was sent to an unintended external email address and may cover approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and notification obligations remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The Disclosure Letter correctly stops short of establishing access, a confirmed breach, notification duty or loss. We should not assert any of those matters without evidence. Equally, the Seller’s expectation of immateriality is unsupported and should not close the issue.

**Pushback:**

- Require immediate preservation of logs, emails, access records, exported files and investigation materials.
- Require a properly scoped investigation and regular written updates.
- Require prompt notice of access evidence, affected data, regulator or individual communications, containment steps and any legal assessment of notification duties.
- Prohibit deletion or alteration of relevant evidence.
- Allocate responsibility for pre-Completion investigation and remediation without assuming a numeric claim or price deduction at this stage.
- Preserve relevant warranties and remedies; do not allow the general disclosure to neutralise them before the facts are known.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts:** Three renewals total AUD 330,000. The current record does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That characterisation is not established by the disclosed facts. Conversely, the amount should not automatically be treated as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Review the renewal terms, service periods, invoices, cancellation rights, accounting treatment, timing and consistency with historical practice. Then determine whether the amounts belong in normal working capital, are Seller obligations, or require another specific adjustment. Avoid both automatic Debt classification and untested acceptance as ordinary course.

### 15. Tax and general IP positions

**Seller position:** Settled under the general regime.

**Departure:** Tax and IP remain open. A counterparty assertion does not settle them, and the general regime must not silently govern them.

**Pushback:**

- Continue separate negotiation of the tax covenant, tax warranties, IP warranties and relevant indemnities.

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves ownership of 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof of title, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:** Require a complete title package, including, as applicable:

- share certificates and issuance/transfer history;
- consistency checks against corporate filings and constitution;
- Seller corporate approvals and execution authority;
- searches and releases concerning security interests or other encumbrances;
- confirmation of no options, convertibles, trusts, beneficial interests or third-party rights; and
- Completion transfers and updated registers.

This evidence supplements rather than replaces the title warranties and 100% fundamental liability regime.

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale

The current disclosures indicate only:

- an office lease notification obligation, not necessarily landlord consent; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction that may not be engaged by a share sale.

We should verify the operative language and comply with any notice requirements, but should not assume consents or price adjustments are required merely from the Seller’s document descriptions. Appropriate no-breach and contracts warranties should remain.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Completion-critical items

1. Effective Bluefen consent, with all conditions satisfied and evidenced.
2. Current Riverlark payout, direct repayment and effective releases at Completion.
3. Clear Seller-funded treatment of the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all triggered on-costs.
4. Ironquay payment/title cure and a broadened specific indemnity.

6. Independent title and encumbrance evidence.

### SPA liability package

1. AUD 6 million general warranty cap.
2. AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
3. Twenty-four-month general claims period.
4. Separate 100%/six-year minimum title and fundamental regime.
5. Mandatory fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs.
6. General limitations confined to general warranties.
7. Separate treatment for tax, IP, specific indemnities, payments and covenants.

### Disclosure and diligence

1. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and constructive disclosure.
2. Delete the broad Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
3. Assess each specific disclosure against the relevant warranty and fair-disclosure standard.
4. Refresh the data room and disclosures through Completion.
5. Investigate Sandbar without automatically treating it as either Debt or ordinary-course cost.

None of the Seller’s descriptions—“agreed,” “adequate,” “settled,” “ordinary course” or “not expected to be material”—should be treated as an agreed Buyer position or verified factual conclusion.
